I would give 4.5, so I rounded up. I’ve begun a journey to learn some Biblical Hebrew and to understand the Word of God more deeply, and this app has many great features for that: side by side viewing of any two (available) translations, created highlights and various underlines, written notes that can be grouped in desired categories, and just overall quality-of-life features like changing the background and text colors with flexibility.

I have a small suggestion to include an optional toggle for the cantillation marks in the Hebrew translation (assuming it’s possible). I understand that I can see them when I click on an individual verse and parse the words of that verse with the concordance, but it’s a bit cumbersome to do that when trying to read through several verses or a whole chapter at a time.

Also, I’m not sure if it’s just on my phone, but I have issues with renaming & changing the color of highlights I’ve created. The changes never save. The only way I can make the change is if I delete the highlight entirely and create a new one with the changes I wanted.

Overall, fantastic app! May our Father God and our Lord Jesus Christ continue to bless you for making His word so accessible! Peace be with you.

I've used em ALL, Blue Letter is the best bible app.. A few things I love about BLB:

1. the variety of English versions: KJV, NKJV, Young's Literal, original NASB, NASB 2020, NIV, NLT, NET, HCSB, Brenton's English translation of the LXX etc 

2. the variety of other languages: several Spanish translations including 16th cent SE / Osos, RVR 1909 & 1960, EM, also has Segond French, Luther's German, Arabic, Russian, Chinese, Latin, and on and on 

3. the variety of Greek manuscript traditions: Byzantine Maj, Scrivener's TR (though I'd prefer Stephanus), MGNT (essentially like the UBS/Nestle Aland), Westcott & Hort, LXX (OT) 

4. It's very very easy to drill down within a verse to a single key Greek or Hebrew word, then pivot from there to any of its other usages in the text. It's almost like a game. 

5. Includes parsing, several lexicon entries (old & new), and all kinds of other study tools WITHOUT feeling like they're intrusive into a simple reading experience. 

6. Parallel translation display. I'll often put Hebrew Masoretic on the left and Greek LXX to the right reading th OT. To see the Latin or English it's always just two clicks away. 

7. It's free and there are no ads. I do recommend donating tho to keep it that way.
